title: Adding and subtracting from a line plot

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Kai measures nine twigs for a model nest, to the nearest quarter inch.

do.text: Nine twig lengths, measured in inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Look between one inch and two inches. Four equal spaces make one inch.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each small step is one fourth of an inch. This twig reaches one and one fourth.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So a length can have a whole number and a fraction together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine measurements. Each gets one *X* at its length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One and one fourth moves to its position, and becomes one *X*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three twigs measure one and three fourths. Move each measurement to that length. Three separate *X* marks stack up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two twigs measure two inches. Their measurements become two *X* marks.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two measure two and a half. Those measurements become two more *X* marks.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One measures three and three fourths. Its measurement becomes the last *X*.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: There is no twig at one and a half. Do I skip that tick?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep it. An empty position means zero twigs of that length. The spaces on the number line stay equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine measurements, nine *X* marks. Each *X* remembers a twig.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: If Kai lays all the two-and-a-half-inch twigs end to end, how long is the row?

do.text: How long is the joined row?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I see two *X* marks. So I need two twigs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Bring the first *X* down. It stands for this whole twig.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Bring the second down. Another two and a half inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide them end to end, with no gap and no overlap.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is the row up close. Two whole inches from each twig make four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The two extra halves lift from the ends, and join to make one more inch.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four whole inches, and one more. Five inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The *X* marks counted twigs. The ruler tells the total length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: How much longer is the longest twig than the shortest?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Use the outermost *X* marks, not the ends of the axis. The longest is three and three fourths; the shortest is one and one fourth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Bring those twigs down, and line up their left ends.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The extra part sticks out. That is the difference!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Greatest minus least gives the range.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count in fourths. The long twig is fifteen fourths. The short twig is five fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fifteen fourths minus five fourths leaves ten fourths. The pieces are still fourths of an inch.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten fourths make two whole inches and two fourths. Two and a half inches.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three and three fourths is the longest length. The range is only the extra part.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: If the question asks for their combined length, join them instead. The same twigs make five inches altogether.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What about all the twigs at one and three fourths?

do.text: How long are these three twigs together?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The label gives one twig's length. The stack has three twigs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One twig. A second. A third. Each is seven fourths of an inch.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Join all three. Seven fourths, plus seven fourths, plus seven fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That is twenty-one fourths. Twenty fourths make five whole inches, with one fourth left.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three copies of the length. I can also write three times one and three fourths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which twig is in the middle when the lengths are ordered? That length is the median.

do.text: Order every twig from shortest to longest.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Unstack the *X* marks into one row, keeping their order. Repeated lengths each get a place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Set aside the outer pair. Set aside the next pair. Then the next.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more pair leaves the fifth twig: two inches.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The middle twig is not in the tallest stack.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Right. Restore the plot. The length that appears most often is the mode.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One and three fourths appears three times, more than any other length. That is the mode.

do.text:
Stack height: 3 twigs.
Length at that stack: $1\frac34$ inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Lena's ten paper strips, measured to the nearest eighth inch.

do.text: Build the plot from the list

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Match each length in the list to its position. Three and one eighth appears twice: two *X* marks.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three and two eighths appears four times. Four *X* marks at that length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three and three eighths also appears four times. Four *X* marks there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: No strip is exactly three inches, or three and four eighths. Both empty positions get zero.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Zero, two, four, four, zero. The counts add to ten, matching the ten strips.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To choose a matching plot, check every stack. Ten *X* marks alone is not enough.

do.text: Right total AND right position for every X.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Suppose this *X* moves one step to the right. We still have ten, but the measurements no longer match.

do.text: One misplaced X changes the data.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Put it back. Four here, zero there. Every listed strip has exactly one *X* at its own length.

do.text: Every strip has one X at its length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The two tallest stacks tie. Both lengths are modes: three and two eighths, and three and three eighths.

do.text: A tie can give two modes

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each dot is one kitten's weight. Five are shown; six weigh twenty-three pounds together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each weight appears once. There is no mode.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Bring down every measurement: three, three and a half, four, four and a half, five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three and five make eight. Three and a half plus four and a half also make eight. Add the remaining four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The five shown weigh twenty pounds. All six weigh twenty-three. The missing kitten accounts for the gap.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Twenty-three minus twenty is three pounds. That is the sixth kitten's weight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Put its dot at three, above the first kitten's dot. Two kittens have that weight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To find a missing measurement, subtract the shown total from the full total.

do.text: Full total − shown total = missing value

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to Kai's twigs. Two *X* marks, two lengths to join.

do.text: Every X is one real measurement

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Bring them down, and lay them end to end. Five inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every *X* is one real measurement. Bring down the ones you need, then add or subtract.
